pages.title: How to Link Peripherals
pages.text: To link a peripheral, you need a Control Seat on a subspace, an AeroIE peripheral—such as a Basic Thruster—on the same intact subspace, and a Linker. The connection must not cross a bearing, and neither block may have been detached from the physical assembly.$(br2)1. Make sure the Linker is empty. Shift-right-click the air to clear any stored position.$(br2)2. Hold the Linker and Shift-right-click the Control Seat. The Linker records the seat's position.

3. With the Linker, Shift-right-click the peripheral. For peripherals with large models, you must click their core block. This binds the peripheral to the Control Seat.$(br2)While holding a Linker that contains a valid Control Seat, every peripheral linked to that seat is marked with a colored outline and its index within that peripheral type.$(br2)The Control Seat automatically removes a peripheral if it becomes invalid—for example, if it is mined, destroyed, or separated onto another subspace.

pages.title: Fun Fact
pages.text: 1. Early in AeroIE's development, Control Seats were planned to broadcast control data so peripherals could connect automatically without a Linker. The resulting cobblestone-tier network synchronization overhead quickly ended that idea.
